text:
evan_support: FYI, customer reported embeddings parity problem across Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. They say hosted embeddings are 1536-d but Dedicated and Private return 1024-d. Ticket #8742 attached. They see downstream index failures.

priya_ml: Thanks for the heads up. Do we have a repro request from the customer? model name+version, exact API calls, and sample input?

ev an_support: Sent repro steps in ticket: curl to /v1/embeddings with model "redwood-embed-1" (no version suffix), input is short sentences ~50-200 chars. Example payload: `{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":"Why is my vector 1024 instead of 1536?"}`. They included responses from hosted (1536) and from their Dedicated pool (1024).

priya_ml: Hmm, could be model variant mismatch (quantized vs full). Dedicated may have been provisioned with the quantized 1024 variant. Are we pinning semantics to exact model hash on Dedicated/Private?

noah_infra: Quick note: Dedicated pools can run model variants that are storage/latency-optimized. We normally expose the same model name but different artifacts (v1 vs v1-q). If customer didn't pin a model version at create time, routing might pick a compatible but lower-dim variant.

sam_runtime: Adding runtime perspective: embeddings should be deterministic in dimension per model family. If we have a variant using a different embedding head or a different tokenizer/peft head, dims will change. Need to confirm model artifact metadata on the Dedicated instance.

priya_ml: Can we ask the customer for full response headers+body from both endpoints? headers might include `x-model-id`, `x-artifact-hash`, `x-embed-dim`. We recently started returning `x-embed-dim` in responses for debugging.

ev an_support: Customer provided hosted response headers: `x-model-id: redwood-embed-1`, `x-artifact: rwd-embed-1@sha256:abcd1234`, `x-embed-dim: 1536`. Dedicated response headers show `x-artifact: rwd-embed-1-q@sha256:efgh5678`, `x-embed-dim: 1024`.

sam_runtime: That confirms variant mismatch. Why did Dedicated pick `-q` variant? Check rollout policy for their Dedicated cluster. Maybe autoscale/policy swapped to a cheaper variant due to memory constraints.

noah_infra: Looking at deployment records for their Dedicated pool (pool id d-44): last config change 1763329000 by infra-auto-scaler. Autoscaler logs show host oom risk and switched to lower-memory artifact for some nodes at 1763331002. I can paste log snippet:
```
[1763331002] autoscaler: node d-44-node-3 mem_pressure=0.89, selected artifact rwd-embed-1-q@sha256:efgh5678
```

priya_ml: That explains it. The auto-scaler picked a variant with smaller KV cache / smaller head (1024). We need to treat embeddings as a non-backwards-compatible change — customers expect dim parity.

evan_support: Customer is upset because their index pipeline failed and they incurred extra egress/storage costs during reindex. They mentioned billing spike. @tara_billing any quick help?

tara_billing: Can review billing adjustments but need confirmation of impact window and usage numbers. If we caused a silent variant swap, consider crediting the reindex job and waive an incident credit. Open to approvals.

sam_runtime: Action plan suggestion: 1) Temporarily force their Dedicated pool to the hosted artifact hash `abcd1234`. 2) Notify customer and roll back. 3) Add a hard pin option or alert when artifact variants change embed dim. 4) Postmortem.

priya_ml: Agreed. Also add a runtime guard: if `x-embed-dim` differs from model catalog expected dim, reject request with 409 + diagnostic headers unless customer explicitly opts in to variant fallback. That prevents silent regressions.

noah_infra: I'll patch the autoscaler policy and set override for pool d-44 to prefer `abcd1234`. Pushing change now.

embed-checker-bot: Running verification job against pool d-44...

embed-checker-bot: Hosted artifact check: rwd-embed-1@sha256:abcd1234 dim=1536. Dedicated pool current artifact for node-1: rwd-embed-1-q@sha256:efgh5678 dim=1024.

noah_infra: Override applied at 1763332200: pool pinned to abcd1234. Restarting nodes to pick up artifact.

sam_runtime: After restart, please capture a few sample responses and check `x-embed-dim` and vector length. Use the customer's exact inputs to validate index recovery.

evan_support: I sent the customer a short repro guide to run after we confirm: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings` and to paste headers/body.

embed-checker-bot: Post-restart check: node-1 artifact updated to rwd-embed-1@sha256:abcd1234. Sample response vector length=1536.

priya_ml: Good. Also check Private deployments: customer reported Private on-prem showed 1024 too. That likely means their Private package was deployed with the `-q` artifact. We need a migration step and guidance for private customers installing the runtime.

noah_infra: For Private, the installer picks the most recent artifact tag unless a pinned hash is provided. I'll add docs + CLI flag `--artifact-hash` and a preflight check that validates `embed_dim` against catalog.

sam_runtime: We'll add a lightweight check in the API server: on startup log model artifact metadata and `embed_dim`. Also emit a warning if the artifact dim doesn't match the catalog canonical dim.

tara_billing: Regarding the billing complaint: please provide customer usage between 1763328000-1763333000 and a list of reindex jobs. I'll prepare a provisional credit if rollback confirmed.

evan_support: Customer replied: after our note they re-ran one index job and it succeeded (vectors now 1536). They're still concerned about silent swaps. Asked for SLA/contract reassurance.

priya_ml: Next steps: - PR for runtime guard (reject variant with mismatched dim unless opt-in) - Autoscaler policy change to prefer canonical artifact for any model with embed dim - Console UX: show `x-embed-dim` and artifact hash per endpoint - Private installer docs + `--artifact-hash` flag - Billing credit request for this customer

sam_runtime: I'll pick up runtime guard PR. Assign to me.

noah_infra: I'll harden autoscaler and add telemetry that triggers an alert when a pool switches artifact for an embeddings model.

tara_billing: I'll queue the credit review and draft messaging.

evan_support: I'll send a proactive status update to the customer including repro confirmation, rollback time, and expected credit.

priya_ml: Optional: add an E2E check in our CI that validates hosted vs dedicated vs private artifact dims for each model in catalog on deploy. That would catch this before shipping.

evan_support: Customer responded with thanks, wants postmortem and asks to be CC'd. They also asked whether this could cause subtle quality regressions even if dims match — good follow-up item.

sam_runtime: Note: even with same dim, quantization can change embedding values. We'll add a note in model catalog page: "embedding parity" requirement includes artifact hash equivalence for critical index use cases.

embed-checker-bot: Regression test added: run embedding parity check on release jobs.

priya_ml: I'll draft a short post-incident summary after we close tasks.

noah_infra: Change set deployed for pool d-44 at 1763332600. Autoscaler policy updated and alerts created.

evan_support: Thanks all. I'll keep thread open until billing and postmortem tasks are complete. :thumbsup:

sam_runtime: If anyone needs logs or exact commands to reproduce locally, ping me.

tara_billing: Billing request submitted to finance queue 1763333500.

priya_ml: Marking owners: runtime=sam_runtime, infra=noah_infra, billing=tara_billing, support=evan_support.

evan_support: Closing comment: customer will be CC'd on postmortem and we plan to offer a one-time credit.

sam_runtime: Closing when PR merged for reject-on-dim-mismatch (target: 1763410000).

embed-checker-bot: Thread note: incident-type=configuration-parity; severity=low-medium; customer-impact=moderate
